thread.title: NY AG and Gov. investigate Apple about privacy violation FaceTime

author: Good King News
title: NY AG and Gov. investigate Apple about privacy violation FaceTime
text:
New York Attorney General Letitia James and Gov. Andrew Cuomo said on Wednesday that they are launching an investigation into Apple Inc.'s
AAPL, + 6.83%
not alerting its customers about a breach of privacy by its FaceTime service. A recent bug allowed users to receive audio and video from the device of the person they were calling, even before the person accepted or rejected the call, they said in a statement. "New Yorkers should not choose between their private communications and their privacy rights," James said. "This FaceTime violation poses a serious threat to the security and privacy of millions of New Yorkers who have placed their trust in Apple and its products over the years." The authorities accept complaints from customers about the infringement and set up a helpline at 1-800-697-1220 which is open from Monday to Friday from 8.30 am to 4.30 pm. There are reports that the bug came to Apple's attention more than a week before Apple spread the app and took action to disable the app's feature that required a solution, they said. Apple's shares rose 6.7% on Wednesday after the quarterly results. The stock has decreased by 0.9% in the past 12 months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average
DJIA, + 1.77%
what counts as a member has dropped 4% and the S & P 500
SPX, + 1.55%
decreased by 5%.
